Plan Human Validation Sample Size for Prediction-Powered Inference (PPI++)

Source: R/ppi_power.R
ppi_sample_size.Rd

Computes the required number of human-coded validation annotations n_labeled to achieve either a target standard error (target_se) or target two-sided statistical power (power for a given effect) under optimal power-tuned PPI++. Uses exact PPI++ asymptotic variance: $$\mathrm{Var}(\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{PPI++}}) = \frac{\sigma^2}{n}\left(1 - r^2 \frac{N}{n + N}\right),$$ where \(\sigma\) is the single-observation human-only standard error scaling constant (\(\sigma = \mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{human}}\sqrt{n_0}\)), \(r \in [0, 1]\) is the correlation between human and LLM estimating scores, and \(N\) is the unlabeled LLM-coded sample size.

Usage

ppi_sample_size(
  target_se = NULL,
  effect = NULL,
  power = 0.8,
  sd = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  n_total = NULL,
  n_unlabeled = Inf,
  pilot = NULL,
  term = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_n = 20L
)

Arguments

target_se

Optional positive target standard error for the focal parameter. Specify either target_se or effect.

effect

Optional non-zero target effect size for a two-sided Wald test at significance level alpha and target power. Ignored if target_se is supplied.

power

Target statistical power in (alpha, 1) when sizing by effect. Default 0.80.

sd

Positive single-observation SD scaling constant (\(\mathrm{SE}_{\mathrm{human}}\sqrt{n}\)). Inferred from pilot if NULL.

r

Correlation magnitude in [0, 1] between human and LLM scores (or estimating equations). Inferred from pilot if NULL.

n_total

Optional finite total corpus size (n_labeled + n_unlabeled). When supplied, solves n_labeled accounting for the irreducible corpus floor \(\sigma / \sqrt{n_{\mathrm{total}}}\). Mutually exclusive with a finite n_unlabeled.

n_unlabeled

Unlabeled LLM-coded pool size N (default Inf, representing a large unlabeled corpus). Ignored if n_total is supplied.

pilot

Optional pilot "llm_ppi" or continuous "llm_calibration" object from which sd and r are estimated automatically.

term

Optional parameter term name to extract from a multi-term "llm_ppi" pilot object. Defaults to the first non-intercept term.

alpha

Two-sided Type-I error rate in (0, 1). Default 0.05.

min_n

Minimum practical validation sample size floor. Default 20L.

Value

An S3 object of class "llm_ppi_sample_size" containing:

  • feasible: logical indicating whether the target is attainable given n_total.

  • n_labeled: required human validation sample size (integer, or NA if infeasible).

  • n_unlabeled: resulting unlabeled sample size.

  • n_human_only: human annotations required without PPI++.

  • annotations_saved, savings_pct: human annotation savings from PPI++.

  • target_se, achieved_se, achieved_power, effective_n, min_n_total_needed, params.

Details

Parameters (sd, r) may be supplied directly or automatically extracted from a pilot ppi_mean(), ppi_lm(), ppi_glm(), ppi_clustered(), ppi_lmer(), or continuous calibration_metrics() object via pilot.

Examples

# Size a validation subset out of a 2,000-text corpus for 80% power on beta = 0.25
plan <- ppi_sample_size(effect = 0.25, power = 0.80, sd = 1.2, r = 0.82, n_total = 2000)
plan
#> 
#> ── PPI++ Human Validation Sample-Size Plan 
#> Inputs (supplied): sd = 1.200 | r = 0.820 | Target SE = 0.0892
#> Required human validation n = 64 (vs. 181 human-only -> saves 117 annotations,
#> 64.6%)
#> Projected PPI++ SE = 0.0886 | Effective n = 183.3 | Power = 0.805

# Or size directly from a pilot PPI fit on ema_coded
data(ema_coded)
agg <- aggregate_scores(ema_coded, score_col = "llm_score")
pilot_fit <- ppi_lm(human_score ~ x + group, data = agg, pred_col = "llm_score")
ppi_sample_size(target_se = 0.06, n_total = 1500, pilot = pilot_fit, term = "x")
#> 
#> ── PPI++ Human Validation Sample-Size Plan 
#> Inputs (pilot_ppi++): sd = 1.163 | r = 1.000 | Target SE = 0.0600
#> Required human validation n = 20 (vs. 376 human-only -> saves 356 annotations,
#> 94.7%)
#> Projected PPI++ SE = 0.0301 | Effective n = 1489.0
